## Summary
- Add `secondary_github_token` to `run-agent-task` and pass `AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT` from agent workflows.
- Expose the additive token as `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN` while preserving primary `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` behavior.
- Document setup, recommended fine-grained PAT scopes, read-only vs write-capable use, and security guidance.
- Add workflow contract tests for the new input and caller wiring.

## Verification
- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- YAML parse check for workflows/action files
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #312

comments.body: We should rename AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT to be something more general
@sepo-agent /answer so this is just adding the secret there but does it tell the agent to use it in the prompt or?

Yes, this PR does both:

- It plumbs the secret into the runtime as `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN`: [action input/env](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/076f2a7ae13b64cee9e00d44fc2cd7ae00280798/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L66-L69), [run env](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/076f2a7ae13b64cee9e00d44fc2cd7ae00280798/.agent/src/run.ts#L282-L286).
- It also updates the base prompt to tell the agent how to use it: keep normal `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` for this repo, and only opt into the secondary token for explicit cross-repo operations, e.g. `GH_TOKEN="$INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN" gh ...`: [prompt lines](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/076f2a7ae13b64cee9e00d44fc2cd7ae00280798/.github/prompts/_base.md#L27-L30).

So it does **not** automatically replace the agent’s default GitHub auth. The agent has to intentionally use the secondary token for a specific external-repo command.

The main implementation shape is clear: an optional action input, a fixed secret wired through shared workflows, explicit prompt instructions, and doc/test coverage; the one real rubric tension is the still-specific `AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT` naming and the breadth of where the credential is exposed.## Rubrics Review

## Notes

- The PR satisfies the core issue #312 acceptance criteria: primary same-repo auth remains separate, `/install` still uses its own primary token path, and tests assert the secondary token does not replace `github_token`.
- The strongest rubric concern is naming/scope: `secondary_github_token` is general, while `AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT` is specific to one expected use. The maintainer comment asks to rename it to something more general, which aligns with the rubric tension.
- Smallest useful follow-up: rename the repository secret/config surface to a general secondary-token name, while keeping backward compatibility or migration docs if existing users may have adopted `AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT`.

## Findings

- **WARNING:** The implementation exposes `AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT` to every shared agent run. This is simple and consistent, but it expands the blast radius for a powerful optional credential. If the intended model is truly “general secondary GitHub token,” rename the secret accordingly and consider whether all routes need it by default.

## Final Rubric Verdict

PARTIAL

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 076f2a7ae13b64cee9e00d44fc2cd7ae00280798 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #317 implements issue #312 by adding an optional additive GitHub credential exposed as `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- The primary `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` behavior remains separate, and tests now guard that the secondary token does not replace primary auth.
- The PR also documents setup and recommended fine-grained PAT permissions for external repository access.
- The remaining concerns are around authorization scope and public configuration naming before this becomes a stable user-facing surface.

## Review
The core plumbing is sound, but the current PR is not ready to merge because it makes write-capable external repository access available through broad prompt-driven routes without a deterministic authorization check. Reviewers broadly agreed on the naming concern; the main severity difference was that one reviewer treated the broad auth surface as blocking, while others framed it as scope/rubric risk.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| External writes are only prompt-authorized | BLOCKING | `.github/prompts/_base.md` allows external writes when the prompt judges the user request requires them, while the secondary token is passed into broad routes such as `answer`. There is no deterministic target-repo or route-level write authorization check. |
| Install receives the general secondary token | WARNING | The `/install` job already uses `AGENT_INSTALL_PAT` as its dedicated primary token, but now also receives the broader secondary credential. That weakens the install route’s intentionally narrow credential boundary. |
| Secret name is too narrow | WARNING | The public secret is named `AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT`, while the runtime contract is the more general `secondary_github_token` / `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN`. The maintainer already asked for a more general name. |
| Prompt omits empty-token guidance | INFO | The action defaults `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN` to an empty string when unset, but the base prompt does not tell agents to check for that before using it. |

## Progress
- Core additive token plumbing, primary-token separation, docs, and tests are present.
- Issue #312’s non-goal of not replacing `GH_TOKEN` is covered by the implementation and tests.
- Maintainer feedback already acknowledges the naming problem, so I did not duplicate that as a new inline comment.
- Posted two inline comments: one on `.github/prompts/_base.md` for prompt-only external write authorization, and one on `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` for the install-route secondary token.
- No existing inline comments or review threads were present before posting; nothing was resolved or minimized.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>External writes are only prompt-authorized</summary>

**Cause:** The base prompt says the agent may use `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN` for external writes when the user request clearly requires it, and workflows pass the token into broad routes such as `answer`. Sepo’s default access policy can allow `CONTRIBUTOR`, so a write-capable external token could be used without a deterministic external target authorization gate.

**Candidate solutions:** Restrict the generic secondary token to read-only external inspection for now, or add a small policy/helper that validates external write intent, requester authorization, and target repository before the prompt may use the credential for writes.

**Comments:** Issue #312 intentionally allows write-capable external access when configured, so the fix should preserve that capability behind a deterministic guard rather than remove the feature entirely.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Install receives the general secondary token</summary>

**Cause:** `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` passes `secondary_github_token: ${{ secrets.AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT }}` to the install job even though the same job uses `AGENT_INSTALL_PAT` as its dedicated install primary token.

**Candidate solutions:** Pass an empty secondary token for `/install`, omit the input there, or document and test a specific reason install needs both credentials.

**Comments:** This is tied to the selected authorization rubric: the install route should not silently gain a broader downstream credential surface.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Secret name is too narrow</summary>

**Cause:** The public configuration name `AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT` bakes in both “cross-repo” and “PAT”, while the action/runtime API is a generic secondary GitHub token.

**Candidate solutions:** Rename the secret to something like `AGENT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN` or `AGENT_EXTERNAL_GITHUB_TOKEN`, and update workflows, docs, templates, and envelope tests consistently.

**Comments:** The maintainer explicitly requested this rename in the PR discussion.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Prompt omits empty-token guidance</summary>

**Cause:** The action and runtime default `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN` to `""`, but `_base.md` only says the token “may be configured.”

**Candidate solutions:** Add one prompt bullet telling agents that an empty value means the secondary credential is unavailable and should not be used.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The unresolved authorization and naming issues are concrete branch changes and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Add a deterministic guard or narrower contract for secondary-token external writes before agents may use a write-capable token outside the current repo.
- [ ] Stop passing the general secondary token into the `/install` route unless a specific install-route need is documented and tested.
- [ ] Rename `AGENT_CROSS_REPO_PAT` to a more general secondary-token secret name across workflows, docs, templates, and tests.

## Review
The core plumbing is sound, tested, and the earlier NEEDS_REWORK items are resolved at head `0ca081d6ff239b7f36a02fe833f2f6b285bd46ad`. Reviewers differ only on residual severity: rubrics treats broad read-only exposure as acceptable, while Codex flags one missing setup-guide warning as a small security-docs gap.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Private external read access needs requester-scope guidance | WARNING | The setup guide recommends read-only external PAT scopes, but does not say that private-repo read access is still sensitive when exposed to all non-install routes. Users should be told to tighten `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY` or avoid private scopes unless requesters are trusted. |
| Prompt does not guard empty secondary token | INFO | `_base.md` shows setting `GH_TOKEN="$INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN"` for external reads, but does not explicitly say to skip that path when the value is empty. This is a minor prompt hardening point already noted in the earlier synthesis. |

## Progress
- Prior external-write, install-route, and secret-name findings are fixed on the current PR head.
- Resolved two superseded same-agent inline threads: `.github/prompts/_base.md` external-write concern and `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` install-route concern.
- Posted one new inline comment on `.agent/docs/deployment/setup-guide.md` line 90 for the private/non-public read-access guidance gap.
- No comments were minimized, deleted, or replied to.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Private external read access needs requester-scope guidance</summary>

**Cause:** The setup guide says to use a read-only fine-grained PAT for external repositories, and bundled non-install workflows pass that token broadly as `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN`. If that PAT can read private or non-public repositories, any actor allowed to trigger those routes by `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY` could ask the agent to inspect and quote that context.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a short setup-guide note that private/non-public external repo scopes require trusted requesters, a tightened `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY`, or avoiding private scopes entirely.

**Comments:** This is docs-only and safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Prompt does not guard empty secondary token</summary>

**Cause:** The prompt example uses `GH_TOKEN="$INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN"` but the action defaults the input to an empty string when the secret is unset.

**Candidate solutions:** Add one sentence telling agents to skip secondary-token external inspection when `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN` is empty.

**Comments:** This is INFO severity and was already covered in the prior synthesis, so I did not duplicate it with another inline comment.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: One unresolved security-docs warning is a concrete branch change and is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Add setup-guide guidance that private or non-public external repository read access through `AGENT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN` requires trusted requesters, tightened `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY`, or avoiding private scopes.

@sepo-agent /answer for example, let's say we want to use the additional auth token to post a comment in another repo (assuming it has the proper access), does it work?

Not for posting a comment, as this PR is currently written.

It will make the token available as `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN`, but the contract is explicitly **read-only external repo inspection**. The base prompt tells the agent to use it only for external repository inspection and specifically says not to use it for external writes, pushes, workflow dispatches, or non-read API calls: [.github/prompts/_base.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9a9e12923fbf69e484cb7c78d02622afb60f34ad/.github/prompts/_base.md#L27-L30).

So even if `AGENT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN` technically had permission to comment in another repo, the agent should not use this secondary token for that under this PR’s rules. To support “post a comment in another repo”, we’d want a route-specific write credential plus deterministic authorization for that exact write path, then document/test that route separately.
